chapter.title: Installation
chapter.para: &zebra; is written in &acro.ansi; C and was implemented with portability in mind. We primarily use GCC on UNIX and Microsoft Visual C++ on Windows.
The software is regularly tested on Debian GNU/Linux, Ubuntu Linux, MAC OSX, Windows.

&zebra; can be configured to use the following utilities (most of which are optional):
&yaz; (required)
&zebra; uses &yaz; to support &acro.z3950; / &acro.sru;. Zebra also uses a lot of other utilities (not related to networking), such as memory management and XML support.
For the DOM XML / ALVIS record filters, &yaz; must be compiled with Libxml2 and Libxslt support and Libxml2 must be version 2.6.15 or later.
iconv (optional)
Character set conversion. This is required if you're going to use any other character set than UTF-8 and ISO-8859-1 for records. Note that some Unixes has iconv built-in.
Expat (optional)
&acro.xml; parser. If you're going to index real &acro.xml; you should install this (filter grs.xml). On most systems you should be able to find binary Expat packages.
Tcl (optional)
Tcl is required if you need to use the Tcl record filter for &zebra;. You can find binary packages for Tcl for many Unices and Windows.
Autoconf, Automake (optional)
GNU Automake and Autoconf are only required if you're using the CVS version of &zebra;. You do not need these if you have fetched a &zebra; tar.
Docbook and friends (optional)
These tools are only required if you're writing documentation for &zebra;. You need the following Debian packages: docbook, docbook-xml, docbook-xsl, docbook-utils, xsltproc.

section.title: UNIX
section.para: On Unix, GCC works fine, but any native C compiler should be possible to use as long as it is &acro.ansi; C compliant.

Unpack the distribution archive. The configure shell script attempts to guess correct values for various system-dependent variables used during compilation. It uses those values to create a Makefile in each directory of &zebra;.

To run the configure script type:
./configure

The configure script attempts to use C compiler specified by the CC environment variable. If this is not set, cc or GNU C will be used. The CFLAGS environment variable holds options to be passed to the C compiler. If you're using a Bourne-shell compatible shell you may pass something like this:
CC=/opt/ccs/bin/cc CFLAGS=-O ./configure

The configure script support various options: you can see what they are with
./configure --help

Once the build environment is configured, build the software by typing:
make

If the build is successful, two executables are created in the sub-directory index:
zebrasrv
The &acro.z3950; server and search engine.
zebraidx
The administrative indexing tool.
index/*.so
The .so-files are &zebra; record filter modules. There are modules for reading &acro.marc; (mod-grs-marc.so), &acro.xml; (mod-grs-xml.so) , etc.

note.para: Using configure option --disable-shared builds &zebra; statically and links "in" &zebra; filter code statically, i.e. no .so-files are generated

section.para:
You can now use &zebra;. If you wish to install it system-wide, then as root type
make install
By default this will install the &zebra; executables in /usr/local/bin, and the standard configuration files in /usr/local/share/idzebra-2.0. If shared modules are built, these are installed in /usr/local/lib/idzebra-2.0/modules. You can override this with the --prefix option to configure.

section.title: GNU/Debian Linux on amd64 Platform
section.para: Index Data provides pre-compiled GNU/Debian and Ubuntu packages at our Debian package archive, both for recent releases.

For Debian, refer to
for how to configure APT. For Ubuntu, refer to . After refreshing the package cache with the command
apt-get update
as root, the &zebra; indexer is easily installed issuing
apt-get install idzebra-2.0 idzebra-2.0-doc

section.title: GNU/Debian and Ubuntu on other architectures
section.para:
These &zebra; packages are specifically compiled for GNU/Debian Linux systems and Ubuntu. Installation on other GNU/Debian systems is possible by re-compilation the Debian way: you need to add only the deb-src sources lines to the /etc/apt/sources.list configuration file, After refreshing the package cache with the command
apt-get update apt-get build-dep idzebra-2.0
as root, the &zebra; indexer is recompiled and installed issuing
fakeroot apt-get source --compile idzebra-2.0
as normal user. The compiled GNU/Debian packages can then be installed as root issuing
dpkg -i install idzebra-2.0*.deb libidzebra-2.0*.deb

section.title: Windows
section.para: The easiest way to install &zebra; on Windows is by downloading an installer from here. The installer comes with source too - in case you wish to compile &zebra; with different Compiler options.
&zebra; is shipped with "makefiles" for the NMAKE tool that comes with Microsoft Visual C++. Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools has been tested.

Open a Visual Studio developer command prompt for the target architecture, for example the x64 Native Tools Command Prompt. Use the same architecture for &yaz;, &zebra;, and their dependencies. The makefiles select BARCH from the Visual Studio environment variable VSCMD_ARG_TGT_ARCH, falling back to x64 if it is not set. You can override this with nmake BARCH=x86 or nmake BARCH=x64; the compiler environment must match the selected architecture.

Install libxml2, libxslt, ICU, Expat, libiconv, and bzip2 with vcpkg. For an x64 build with vcpkg installed in c:\vcpkg, run:
c:\vcpkg\vcpkg install libxml2:x64-windows libxslt:x64-windows icu:x64-windows expat:x64-windows libiconv:x64-windows bzip2:x64-windows
For an x86 build, use x86-windows instead. The makefiles use the DLL-based vcpkg triplets and expect headers, import libraries, and DLLs under c:\vcpkg\installed\$(BARCH)-windows. If vcpkg is installed elsewhere, adjust the dependency paths in both makefiles.

When building from Git, initialize the submodules in both source repositories before compiling:
git submodule update --init --recursive
In particular, the m4 submodule supplies the Tcl script that generates version information. Ensure that tclsh is on your PATH, or set TCL in the makefiles to its location. The default &yaz; build also uses win_bison to generate its CQL parser.

Place the &yaz; and &zebra; source directories next to each other, named yaz and idzebra. Build &yaz; first, then &zebra;, from their respective win directories:
cd yaz\win nmake cd ..\..\idzebra\win nmake

Customize the build by editing win\makefile or overriding settings on the NMAKE command line.
The following summarizes the most important settings in that file:
DEBUG
If set to 1, the software is compiled with debugging libraries (code generation is multi-threaded debug DLL). If set to 0, the software is compiled with release libraries (code generation is multi-threaded DLL).
BARCH
Target architecture, x86 or x64. This also selects the vcpkg installation directory, as described above.
YAZDIR
Directory of &yaz; source, defaulting to the sibling yaz directory. &zebra;'s makefile expects headers under src, import libraries such as yaz5.lib and yaz_icu5.lib under lib, and DLLs under bin. Debug builds use the corresponding names with a d suffix.
HAVE_EXPAT, EXPAT_DIR
If HAVE_EXPAT is set to 1, &zebra; is compiled with Expat support. EXPAT_DIR defaults to c:\vcpkg\installed\$(BARCH)-windows, with headers in include, libexpat.lib in lib, and libexpat.dll in bin.
HAVE_LIBXML2, LIBXML2_DIR, HAVE_LIBXSLT, LIBXSLT_DIR
Enable libxml2 and libxslt support, including the DOM XML and ALVIS filters. Both are enabled by default, and both directories default to c:\vcpkg\installed\$(BARCH)-windows.
HAVE_ICU, ICU_BASE, ICU_VER
Enable ICU support through &yaz;. ICU is enabled by default, with ICU_BASE set to c:\vcpkg\installed\$(BARCH)-windows. Set ICU_VER to the major version installed by vcpkg so the makefile copies the correct versioned DLLs. Keep this setting consistent with the &yaz; makefile.
HAVE_BZIP2, BZIP2_DIR
BZIP2 record compression support is enabled by default. BZIP2_DIR defaults to c:\vcpkg\installed\$(BARCH)-windows, with bzlib.h in include, bz2.lib in lib, and bz2.dll in bin. Set HAVE_BZIP2=0 to disable this support.

warning.para: The DEBUG setting in the makefile for &zebra; must be set to the same value as DEBUG setting in the makefile for &yaz;. The default is DEBUG=0 in both makefiles.

section.para:
When satisfied with the settings in the makefile, type
nmake

note.para: If the nmake command is not found on your system open a Visual Studio developer command prompt with the C++ build tools installed. This sets the compiler, linker, and Windows SDK environment for the selected target architecture.

section.para:
If you wish to recompile &zebra; - for example if you modify settings in the makefile you can delete object files, etc by running.
nmake clean

The following files are generated upon successful compilation:
bin/zebraidx.exe
The &zebra; indexer.
bin/zebrasrv.exe
The &zebra; server.

These paths are relative to the &zebra; source directory. The build also copies the &yaz; and vcpkg runtime DLLs into bin, including the libxml2 dependencies zlib and libiconv. Keep these DLLs alongside the executables when running or copying them to another directory.

section.title: Upgrading from &zebra; version 1.3.x
section.para:
&zebra;'s installation directories have changed a bit. In addition, the new loadable modules must be defined in the master zebra.cfg configuration file. The old version 1.3.x configuration options
# profilePath - where to look for config files profilePath: some/local/path:/usr/share/idzebra/tab
must be changed to
# profilePath - where to look for config files profilePath: some/local/path:/usr/share/idzebra-2.0/tab
# modulePath - where to look for loadable zebra modules modulePath: /usr/lib/idzebra-2.0/modules

note.para: The internal binary register structures have changed; all &zebra; databases must be re-indexed after upgrade.

section.para:
The attribute set definition files may no longer contain redirection to other fields. For example the following snippet of a custom custom/bib1.att &acro.bib1; attribute set definition file is no longer supported:
att 1016 Any 1016,4,1005,62
and should be changed to
att 1016 Any

Similar behaviour can be expressed in the new release by defining a new index Any:w in all &acro.grs1; *.abs record indexing configuration files. The above example configuration needs to make the changes from version 1.3.x indexing instructions
xelm /*/alternative Body-of-text:w,Title:s,Title:w xelm /*/title Body-of-text:w,Title:s,Title:w
to version 2.0.0 indexing instructions
xelm /*/alternative Any:w,Body-of-text:w,Title:s,Title:w xelm /*/title Any:w,Body-of-text:w,Title:s,Title:w

Server installations which use the special &acro.idxpath; attribute set must add the following line to the zebra.cfg configuration file:
attset: idxpath.att
